summary.prose: Temporary connections belong to a workbench session and a selected repository, with configuration and credentials kept in memory. Panel closure or repository switching preserves them; workbench end,90-second lease loss or daemon restart expires them. S003 supplies the daemon protocol and isolated runtime, while S005 supplies the manager and lifetime explanation. LLM analysis uses an admitted local daemon route; unverified MCP reasoning and query-embedding retrieval/lineage modes fail explicitly.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a daemon-owned application service over the existing repository JSON registry and driver implementations. Separate saved commit, runtime activation and client refresh; use immutable credential generations and atomic JSON replacement rather than pretending the filesystem and keychain share a transaction. Temporary configurations remain in daemon memory under a workbench lease. All descriptions below are proposed architecture, not assertions of current implementation.

boundary.internal: Session open/resume/heartbeat/end, memory-only temporary overlays and receipts, trusted execution-context propagation through analyzer/tool/MCP call paths, expiry and saved/temporary collision rules. Bind the S001-owned sc8 file execution policy to session identity and expiry; S001 owns conversion, cache-policy isolation and private DuckDB lifecycle. Every native/converted kind uses that foundation rather than a branch-local converter.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Safe saved-config read/patch, canonical repo validation, driver profiles, registry metadata/receipts and crash recovery, immutable secret generation staging, compatibility adapters and lease accounting foundation. Does not own temporary storage or rich manager layout. Preserve saved-only scope-local lookup and legacy pinned-family values; signed operation tickets make expiry/replay decidable after receipt pruning. Own the shared memory-only conversion/probe driver foundation, converter-cache policy/identity changes and private DuckDB lifecycle (sc8), completed before the S002/S003 branches.
Transient process probe transport, deadline/cancellation and sanitization. Uses foundational context slots without depending on s3’s session implementation.
Removal coordination for both scopes, busy/revision enforcement, confirmation state, postcommit credential cleanup retry and operation-status recovery. Never invokes source data deletion.

Settings contributions and shared command routing, themed editor/forms, filters, dirty guards, stale-test suppression and truthful feedback in extension and external IDE. HLD has inspected the external pane, actions, service, mirrored types and Settings registrations; S005 implements the recorded plan and validates its mirrored contract before integration acceptance.

nonFunctional.performance: Draft tests have a 10-second parent-enforced deadline, with forced child reap if graceful termination fails. Workbench heartbeat is 30 seconds and expiry 90 seconds after last valid heartbeat. Mutations serialize per repo; list/filter work does not perform driver probes. LLD load tests must verify no leaked children, leases or session entries after cancellation/expiry.
nonFunctional.security: Daemon owns every saved/temporary config and credential decision; client labels/PIDs are not authorization. Registered-root eligibility gates management and temporary operations; saved-only analysis preserves canonical scope-local lookup without gaining mutation rights. Safe read responses return a profile allowlist and presence booleans only. Secrets, capabilities and full requests never enter logs, receipts, prompts, artifacts, telemetry or checkpoints. Temporary inputs never reach disk or keychain. A test worker receives config via private IPC and may not emit raw driver errors. Temporary file conversion, query spill and metadata/logging are part of the no-persistence boundary, including test workers.
nonFunctional.observability: Use getLogger with operation ID, safe code, repo ID, scope, revision and phase only; timing and counters for commit, activation, recovery, timeout, busy refusal and session expiry. No raw exceptions or endpoint/options. Operation status exposes committed truth even when response delivery or activation failed. Recovery-required and cleanup-pending are visible and actionable.
nonFunctional.durability: Saved JSON remains authoritative. Same-directory atomic rename/fsync commits registry, revisions and receipts together; immutable keychain generations preserve previous effective credentials until commit. Recover preparation records before enabling mutation. Issue signed 30-day operation tickets; preserve receipts through ticket expiry and pending cleanup, and distinguish expired-unreceipted from valid-not-seen after restart. Temporary state and receipts expire on explicit session end, 90-second lease loss or daemon epoch change.

preconditions: sc5 methods are proposed additions, not existing support. Use a fixed private RPC family db.connections.v2.session.open/resume/attach/heartbeat/end. End by handle is an internal function; public end accepts no arbitrary handle and derives it from the authenticated transport.

Open creates a random256-bit handle, separate random256-bit bearer capability and random session-memory HMAC key; only capability digest is retained for constant-time verification. Dedicated control transport attachment survives transient reconnect through resume; data/MCP transports use attach and cannot renew the lease.

Canonical registered-root eligibility is required for each temporary management operation and overlay. One session may own overlays for multiple eligible roots; panel/repo switch never ends it. No authorization from PID/client label/chat ID.
Session methods and all session-bound data work route to main daemon, not worker-thread stores. A daemon-owned immutable access context is bound to request lifetime and validated again after awaits.

Control and data authority use DISTINCT role-bound capability digests. Open/resume returns only control capability; new strict db.connections.v2.session.delegate on the current control transport validates canonical registered repoRoot and mints a data-only SessionResume token bound to session/root/control-generation. Private MCP bootstrap passes only that data token. session.attach accepts SessionResume plus exact repoRoot and never accepts a control token. Resume accepts only the control capability; data tokens cannot resume, delegate, heartbeat or end, even on a fresh socket. No role comes from a client-supplied label. Bound32 active delegation tokens per session; expired/revoked tokens are removed and quota refusal is busy.

Data delegation audience is selected only by current authenticated control and stored server-side. Workbench MCP launcher always receives mcp-unverified, never workbench-ui or control capability. Unverified MCP reasoning/data egress has no supported temporary mode in S003; deny before runner, continuation load, trace, prompt, result or error-evidence construction.
postconditions: Open/resume returns heartbeatMs30000/leaseMs90000. Heartbeat is accepted only on current control generation; resume atomically increments generation and detaches the old control transport. An exactly-at-deadline request expires before authorization; only a valid pre-deadline heartbeat extends the monotonic deadline.

Temporary create/update/status/ticket/read/list/activation bind existing sc1/sc2 keys and schema; ticket signature binds session via its private memory key, request HMAC covers full canonical payload, and receipts contain only safe outcomes. Same-ID changed-payload replay rejects. Session expiry invalidates all tickets/receipts regardless of wall clock.

register resolves Keep only from selected immutable in-memory generation; Replace/Clear update private data only. Never call resolveConfigSecrets/keychain/list/load/adoption or any registry writer for temporary state. Paths use existing prepareRuntimeConfig. New ID/kind/family immutable per existing profile rules.

Create/update commits memory entry + revision + receipt atomically under the same root gate as saved ID reservation. Activation is afterward; failure does not erase committed truth. Existing active leases refuse update; no user remove workflow in S003.

End/lease expiry first closes admission and detaches every transport; cancels owned runs/probes/conversion and synchronously prevents further resolution; drops capabilities/receipts/config secret references, then awaits active operations and owned close. Failures leave a closed cleanup record with only owned runtime handles and safe counters; no success reported while a child/resource remains. Daemon shutdown awaits drains; process restart has no recoverable temporary state.

Limit64 live sessions,64 connections/session,8MiB cumulative serialized config/session and16384 receipts/session; return existing busy on quota before committing, never evict live receipts silently. Per temporary file resource uses existing sc8 memoryBudgetBytes256MiB/allowSpillfalse; file source/data/config/capability material never goes to temp/cache/logs. Budgets are fixed internal limits, not a UI option. JS garbage collection limits mean logical erasure rather than guaranteed physical zeroization.

Control resume revokes old-generation data attachments/delegations after canceling their in-flight work, preserving overlay state. Current control can re-delegate over the existing private child control pipe; each forwardStep attaches its fresh socket with the current root-bound data token. Lost/revoked bootstrap fails session-expired until refreshed, never saved-only fallback. Parent/workbench lifetime integration remains S005; sc5 owns only this protocol and backend authority.

A workbench-ui audience can invoke admitted daemon-owned one-shot and deterministic data operations; mcp-unverified receives only safe metadata/fixed refusal, never session data/config/derived reports. All step phases and final/partial/progress/error channels enforce this distinction.

### Root-bound connection-scope resolution

The session data attachment is bound to exactly one canonical selected lookupRoot, chosen at authenticated attach and revalidated for registered-root eligibility. Panels/root switches create or reattach a data channel to the selected root while the same workbench session owns its other overlays. Scope IDs emitted by a model do not select a different root. connectionIsRegistered must check the visible saved+temporary entries at this root through the live resolver, and resolveConnection must return that root plus the selected ID/revision. It never enumerates other repositories in session mode. If a temporary-only ID is absent/expired, report not-found/session-expired; a same-name saved ID elsewhere must remain invisible. Existing unattached saved ambiguity and own-directory semantics stay unchanged. [[c15]]

Proposed additive signatures: resolveScope(ref, deps?, execution?); resolveScopeForTarget(ref, target, deps?, table?, execution?); connectionIsRegistered(id, deps?, execution?); resolveTaskScope(ref, family, templateLabel, deps?, table?, execution?); prepareScope(mode, inputs, deps?, execution?); stepScope(intent, deps?, execution?). ClassifyDriverArgs gains readonly connectionAccess/executionPolicy; connectionCheckFor uses an owner-derived checker for session work, including target-hint bypass and injected checker tests. Existing arguments and defaults remain for unattached calls; the session-memory binding itself makes omitted carrier an error. Data-target child scopes outside the attachment root are refused before measurement, lookup or provider calls. Code/docs/infra keep their graph semantics and the same nonpersistent execution policy.

### Streaming maintenance and recursive execution

holdingForward must distinguish response delivery from actual handler settlement. For any request with a lifetime, neither a done/error frame nor socket cancellation releases the real maintenance shared hold. directDispatch settles the handler, seals/completes RequestLifetime in finally, and the entry wrapper awaits completed AND drained. A refusal before dispatch completes an empty lifetime without constructing a driver. Legacy no-lifetime callers and genuine subscription exceptions retain their behavior; session data work is not a subscription exception. Tests acquire the enabled exclusive maintenance lock while a real stream has sent its terminal frame, disconnected, or thrown on delivery, and prove exclusion until delayed owned cleanup settles. RunAnalyzeOpts, PlanBuilderOpts, RecursivePlannerArgs.opts and all downstream options carry the SAME immutable connectionAccess/executionPolicy; user input does not carry them. The owner supplies a memory-only run-record port. runAnalyze validates before runStages reads any resume record, and scopes live accounting/status/cancel to (owner,root,runId). runStages forwards policy into classification, target-hint checks, measureRequestScope, prepareScope/buildRunBundle, recursive planner and executor. completeRun, outer error handling and interrupted-run repair use the owner port rather than readRunRecord/writeRunRecord. Recursive walk explicitly includes policy in fresh planArgs, childMeasure options, child scope checks and recursive invocation; childInput has no secret authority. Before every child and final publication revalidate session and used revisions. A returned report/status may be read only by the authenticated owner; no terminal/error branch writes to durable run/task/plan/history storage. [[c15]]

### Provider admission contract

This is an S003 integration guard around the existing LLMProvider abstraction, not a new cloud provider or a change to model tiering. Proposed internal helper in src/analyze/connection-provider.ts: admitConnectionProvider(candidate: LLMProvider, execution: ConnectionExecutionContext, evidence: ConnectionProviderEvidence): LLMProvider. This helper/file is proposed. It returns a per-run facade implementing the existing interface; caller-supplied kind strings, function flags or JSON cannot authorize a provider. The owner maintains a WeakMap identity registration and bounded immutable evidence records tied to exact adapter source/compiled digests, provider kind/version, role/model, loopback endpoint and tested request/trace/retry configuration. All required assertions must be true: no prompt/output/history/cache/failure-file writes, no raw error/payload logs, cancellation and drain propagate, and every retry revalidates authority. Missing/stale proof rejects unsupported-temporary before prompt construction/submission. [[c16]]

Supported S003 mode is narrowly 'ollama-local-memory': only a locally selected Ollama provider, loopback host, no persistent request history/trace, with both adapter tests and an isolated actual-service smoke proving the configured server's no-history/no-prompt-log behavior. A mocked SDK is insufficient release evidence. Production admission starts empty until that evidence passes. Current Claude/Codex CLI modes are explicitly unsupported for session-derived prompts; reject BEFORE temporary schema/failure files or subprocess spawn. No currently supported CLI no-history mode is claimed. A future nonpersistent CLI mode requires its own reviewed proof rather than a guessed flag. Preserve role resolution/model/coreFloor; if the selected candidate is disallowed, report the limitation instead of silently choosing a cheaper/weaker/local alternative. Deterministic session data operations may still run without an LLM. Saved-only work retains existing provider behavior.

Guard every direct/injected/factory path listed below. buildShaperProvider/resolveRoleProvider gain an optional final execution argument; RunAggregatorArgs, DecomposeArgs, synthesis/narrow/classifier/planner/tool-loop arguments forward it explicitly. Guard before building data-bearing messages, and at complete/completeStructured entry plus EVERY internal SDK/structured-output retry and stream attempt; session-derived embedding is refused before backend selection or submission. A run-bound Ollama instance or adapter owns the request guard; never attach mutable owner state to the shared role-router cache. An injected provider without owner-issued identity proof is rejected before its method executes. A pre-admitted factory failure, admission failure or expired binding is nonretryable across provider kinds; only a transient failure of the same admitted mode may retry under live authorization. No direct cloud REST/SDK is introduced. Cancellation is propagated to the actual request; registerDrain retains maintenance exclusion until request/stream closes. Only safe fixed error codes reach runtime mapping or logs.

Required integration proves guard is reached for classification, target-hint path, planning/recurse, decomposition, narrow probes, synthesis, adherence, aggregation and legacy read-only tool loop; denial counters are zero for send, spawn, schema/failure-file creation and raw injected-provider method calls. Cover expiry between attempts, structured retries, streaming cancellation, late response, role-router cache reuse across two owners, configured CLI selection and injected providers that lie about kind. Background summarization/indexing and persistence-capable tools are refused before enqueue/provider use when carrying session-derived data. Existing background providers are unchanged.

### Canonical management namespace and explicit alias-upsert refusal

Registry identity is the EXACT supplied lookup path string, not merely the physical directory: repoIdOf hashes that string and connectionsPath selects its hashed saved target. A symlink, trailing-slash, relative or other noncanonical string can therefore name a different legacy saved registry even when it resolves to the same filesystem directory. A canonical mutex does not merge these registries. The earlier draft's promise to keep alias writes targeting their old registry while enforcing physical-root-wide duplicate rejection in both orders was incorrect and is removed. S003 does not add a reverse alias index, scan/merge unknown saved targets, or migrate legacy registrations. [[c26]]

The collision domain is the VISIBLE management context required by DEF S003/ac1: (exact canonical registered lookupRoot, saved rows at connectionsPath(lookupRoot), this session's temporary overlay at that same root). Canonical temporary admission checks that saved target under the shared root gate; saved canonical create checks every active/draining temporary reservation at the same canonical target. Same temporary IDs across separate workbenches remain allowed, with saved create blocked while either canonical reservation remains. This is not a claim of unique IDs across every path-string registry that happens to resolve to the same physical directory. Alias/nested/unregistered saved-only contexts are separate existing lookup namespaces and are never automatically merged into the canonical manager. [[c27]]

Explicit refusal rule: while the S003 owner is installed for a registered canonical root (including closing/draining state), saveConnectionRpc must validate the requested path identity BEFORE savedManagementFor lookup, secret extraction or registry access/writes. If realpath(input) identifies that registered root but input is not its EXACT canonical registered string, reject the legacy upsert with the existing fixed invalid-input error and guidance to use canonical registered repository management. Do not silently replace input with canonicalRoot and write a different registry; do not inspect/adopt/mutate the alias registry. All v2 and temporary management already require the exact canonical registered key and reject aliases. Routing still sends these saved writers to the main owner before any worker executes them. An older/gated-off daemon with no installed or possible temporary state preserves its existing legacy behavior. A nested/unregistered own-directory registry is never promoted to its containing registered root.

This refusal applies to new registration/upsert attempts that can introduce IDs; it is not a S004 removal redesign. Existing legacy saved-only reads remain exact-path and unchanged, including preexisting alias targets. Existing legacy removal behavior remains classified in S004/S001, creates no new ID and cannot delete private temporary state. The manager never shows an old alias row as a canonical-root row or offers it a temporary overlay. A future explicit alias-registry migration/physical-root-wide uniqueness policy requires its own upstream design and user-visible migration, not this Story.

Preexisting alias records are therefore handled explicitly, without pretending their unknown path hashes can be reversed. A record stored through alias A before S003 remains readable ONLY through saved-only lookupRoot A; it is not a row in canonical management context C. Temporary(C,id) may use the same ID if Saved(C,id) is absent, because Saved(A,id) is not visible in C. An attached session requesting A is rejected rather than merged, redirected or allowed a temporary overlay. Unattached A still resolves its own saved source, never Temporary(C,id); canonical C resolves only Saved(C,*) plus its own session overlay, never Saved(A,*). Thus neither source can shadow or leak into the other's context. No canonical-temporary rejection is falsely promised for that separate preexisting namespace. This replaces the earlier erroneous alias-saved-first/canonical-temp rejection test; the new protocol refuses alias upsert BEFORE it can commit, while compatibility coverage proves old separate targets remain isolated.

edgeCases.input: Same temporary ID in sessions A and B at the same root

edgeCases.input: Heartbeat arrives exactly at deadline or wall clock moves

alternativesConsidered.name: Session registry with owned in-memory entries
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One daemon session registry owns separate per-repository overlays of immutable temporary entries.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Smallest complete sc5 shape: daemon issues workbench handle/capability and keeps a memory-only session record with repo overlays, credentials and receipts. Each overlay implements the existing ConnectionResolver callback contract using the foundational lease gate, driver factories, materializeDraft and sc8 memory-only resource policy; it never registers into the saved pool. Trusted transport attachment and an explicit execution-context carrier provide access without changing wire MutationRequest/ConnectionKey semantics. Saved ID reservation and temporary commit share the existing per-root mutation coordinator. S004 consumes an internal lifecycle/removal port and S005 consumes the session protocol; no UI, converter or saved persistence redesign.
pros: Strong ownership and exact memory-only boundary with no saved loader/keychain paths in temporary construction.
Fits existing sessionOverlay resolver injection and S002 prepareTemporary hook.
Minimum new state: session, repo overlay, entry, receipt and active-use records.
cons: Must implement temporary entry lifecycle over existing lease primitives rather than reusing every DriverPool internal.
Requires complete consumer/context propagation inventory; incomplete graph alone is insufficient.

alternativesConsidered.name: One injected DriverPool per session and repository
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each overlay delegates runtime entries to a pool whose configuration and secret providers are entirely in memory.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep the same sc5 session/capability protocol and sc1/sc2/sc3/sc8 contracts, but add explicit configuration-source and credential-source ports to DriverPool; instantiate one isolated temporary pool per session/repository. The saved default providers retain existing behavior, while the temporary providers have no disk/keychain capability. Memory-only policy identity uses session/repo/revision and session end closes the owned pool. Registry/tickets/receipts remain in the sc5 memory owner. This is an additive integration at the S001 pool port, requiring owner compatibility review rather than redesign of saved contracts.
pros: Reuses current pool construction/idle-close and callback lease mechanics.
Single familiar runtime abstraction for saved and temporary drivers.
cons: Broader changes to S001-owned pool internals and stronger proof against accidental reload/secret fallback required.
Current pool build calls saved secret resolution and reload paths, so injecting only a factory would be insufficient.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Protocol is compatible, but memory-only and lifecycle safety depend on broader changes to saved-pool internals; not the smallest complete integration.

erDefinition.narrative: Shows memory ownership and reusable delegation authority. A session owns overlays, at most one control transport and bounded data delegations; each delegation can outlive a socket and owns zero or many data transports. Every data transport has exactly one delegation; control transports have none.

WorkbenchConnectionSession.description: One daemon-epoch workbench lifetime; capability digest and signing key remain in memory.

handle.description: Opaque random session identifier, never persisted.

overlays.description: Zero or more repository overlays exclusively owned by this session.

delegations.description: Zero to32 root/generation-bound data-only authority tokens owned by session; control capability is separate.

controlAttachment.description: Zero or one current control transport; control has no data delegation.

RepositoryOverlay.description: Exactly one session and one canonical registered root; no saved registry ownership.

entries.description: Temporary connection generations owned by this session/root.

receipts.description: Safe memory-only mutation outcomes retained through session lifetime.

TemporaryEntry.description: One isolated temporary ID/revision and private credentials; owns runtime resource.

resource.description: At most one constructed owned driver/private file resource for current generation.

TemporaryReceipt.description: One session/root operation result and request HMAC; never contains plaintext credentials.

RuntimeResource.description: Private driver/lease boundary; never shared with saved pool or another session.

DataDelegation.description: One server-memory data audience/root/control-generation binding; cannot resume, heartbeat, end or delegate.

lookupRoot.description: Exactly one canonical registered repository permitted for this delegation.

attachments.description: Zero or more fresh or overlapping data transports using this token; each data transport has exactly one delegation.

audience.description: Server-stored workbench-ui or mcp-unverified output audience, chosen by authenticated control; cannot be promoted by attached child.

ControlTransportAttachment.description: Current workbench control generation; no data delegation owns it.

DataTransportAttachment.description: One authenticated data socket owned by exactly one root/audience-bound delegation; unverified reasoning audience cannot export session outputs.

lookupRoot.description: Must equal its owning delegation canonical root.
